name: Cedar & Grain
headline:
A better boundary.
A place to stay awhile.
intro: Privacy, gathering space and the details that make a yard feel like yours. Explore a thoughtful approach to fences, decks and outdoor carpentry.
about_title: Built around how you want to use the space.
about_body: Cedar & Grain is a fictional outdoor-carpentry brand. Its starting point is the way a space should work: the view, the privacy, the route through the yard and the place where everyone gathers.
tagline: Space to gather. Details to appreciate.
split_title:
Start with the way
you want to live outside.
split_body: Material choice, dimensions, access and the surrounding property shape a useful project brief. Boundaries, permits and structural requirements are confirmed with the appropriate local professionals.
services: Discuss privacy goals, approximate length, gates, views and material preferences. A real contractor confirms boundaries, local requirements and site conditions before design and installation.
Share goals and measurements, not assumptions about a property line.
Shape a deck brief around seating, circulation, elevation and maintenance preferences. Structure, attachment and required approvals are assessed by qualified professionals.
Note the intended use, access and approximate size.
Review existing fences, deck boards, gates and trim to understand condition and the scope of repair. Cosmetic changes do not establish structural safety.
Ask for an assessment of condition before choosing a repair scope.
steps: Choose the project type and compare sample material considerations.
Confirm dimensions, boundaries, access and local requirements.
Agree materials, layout, scope, timing and payment terms.
faqs: There is no single choice for every property. Compare appearance, maintenance, exposure and budget with the contractor.
Requirements vary by project and location. The actual contractor and local authority should confirm the requirements.
No. The gallery uses illustrative stock scenes to show a presentation style, not work completed by this fictional company.
Is the planning form an estimate?
No. It is a local project brief. A real estimate requires site review and an agreed scope.
gallery_title: Wood, light and room to gather.
note: This sample brief is not a structural assessment, permit review or contractor estimate.
tool_title: Choose the feel. Consider the upkeep.
tool_intro: Compare material considerations and turn a preference into a sample project brief.
proof: Design around privacy, gathering and access.
